message: Delegated tasks require an active run owned by this MCP provider session.
task:
Continue the explicitly authorized OpenAI-proof research in /home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/openai-proof-research. This is a T3-owned round-3 operator task. Read AGENTS.md, sources/upstream.json, sources/CONTENTS.md, frontier/iterations/README.md, frontier/iterations/i02-operator-r2.md and frontier/reviews/i02-crossfield-r2.md. Accept the pinned upstream theorems as true; do not audit upstream truth. User requires a substantial genuinely new theorem or new important MathDB case, not merely technical diagnostics. All source premises must be actual manuscript statements and pinned source identities.

Two sequential goals:
1. Independently audit NEW deductions in i02-operator-r2.md sections 3–7, especially the uniform even-base estimate, global Gaussian bound for V, exact coordinate recurrences for T_a and T_a*, parity disintegration/Fubini, and no-invariant-ideal proof. Also check the comparison supercyclicity and conditional similarity statements. Parent reproduced the finite checks and verified 21 source/literature hashes but that is not a proof audit. Report any corrections explicitly. Do not spend most of the task redoing the already audited rank-one/threshold material.
2. Work on the specified positive infinite-rank T_a=S+M_a V (1<=a<=2) and its ORDINARY closed invariant subspaces. Attempt a concrete invariant half-space with full invariance, nonzero/proper and closure proofs, or a valid new theorem about the class that materially advances the target. Read primary positive-operator and commuting-operator literature early; verify every extra compactness/kernel/Dunford-Pettis assumption rather than assuming positivity+quasinilpotence suffices. Use the exact normalized V, not a truncated normalizer. Explore structural decompositions, scalar-functional separation, analytic orbit closures, or rigorously justified growth-separated subspaces. A closed T-invariant subspace is not necessarily an ideal or S-invariant. No analytic recovery of noncommuting generators is possible from one operator. No fibrewise-to-global cyclicity inference, finite-truncation universal claim, or similarity-to-S construction counts as success. If you find a concrete ordinary invariant subspace, characterize exactly which construction it rules out and what follows; do not call an obstruction a substantial new ISP theorem. If a substantial new candidate emerges, give its full proof and targeted prior-art screen. If no solution, preserve the strongest precise failed argument and gap; do not declare research completed.

Writes ONLY: frontier/reviews/i02-operator-r3.md, frontier/iterations/i03-operator-halfspace.md, frontier/experiments/i03_operator/, frontier/sources/i03_operator/. Do not edit existing reports or shared indexes, stage, commit, change other projects, or spawn more agents. Parent integrates each finding separately. Reuse cached sources where possible and record input/source hashes and primary citations. Return a candid distinction between verified technical deductions, unresolved candidates, and any substantial novel theorem.
